name: Battle of Bands
description:
About the Event:

An incredible opportunity beckons the phenomenal college music teams of India, inviting them to partake in the prestigious Battle of Bands, where they have the chance to claim victory in the ultimate showdown.


Event Details:

Round 1: Online Screening Round

  1. A Google form will be shared with the team head upon contacting any one of the organisers. The form, with team details and a video of the team’s previous performance, must be submitted by 22 February 2026.
  2. The video must be between 2 to 15 minutes long. Live performance videos are preferred (edited videos are not allowed).
  3. Submission must include a minimum of one eastern and one western composition.
  4. Top 6 teams will be shortlisted for the competition based on their Google form submissions.

Round 2: Final Round

  1. The teams selected from the Screening Round will perform on stage for Battle of Bands ‘26.
  2. Performance must include a minimum of one eastern and one western composition.
  3. Each team will be allotted 5 minutes for sound-check and 15 minutes for the performance. Exceeding the 20-minute time limit will result in negative points.


Rules and Regulations:

  1. A team can consist of a minimum of 6 members and a maximum of 12 members on stage, including at least 3 instrumentalists.
  2. All the team members must be from the same college.
  3. Participants must present a physical college ID card and PID to participate in the event.
  4. All participants must be present at the venue at least one hour before the commencement of the event.
  5. Performance order will be decided 30 minutes before the event.
  6. Participants must bring their instruments; only a drum kit will be provided. Backing tracks and synthesized beats are not allowed.
  7. Vulgarity and profanity in any form, will result in disqualification.
  8. Organisers reserve the right to disqualify any team at their discretion without prior notice.
  9. The decisions of the judges and organisers are final and binding.


Judging Criteria:

  • Creativity.
  • Musical Quality.
  • Technical merit.
  • Team synchronization.
  • Stage presence.
  • Bonus marks will be awarded for original composition, musical complexity, and theme integration.

name: Couture
description:
About the Event:

Fashion is not just style; it’s an art of expression, creativity, and making an impression. Couture is the platform to showcase the unseen, unforgettable, and truly spectacular in fashion. Form your team, work around a theme, and own the runway with your ideas, style, and flair. This is your chance to dazzle, impress, and make your fashion statement!

Event Details:

Round 1: Online Screening Round

  1. The team lead will receive a Google form by contacting any of the organisers listed below.
  2. Team leaders must upload portfolios of all team models in PDF format, along with a video of their previous performance, via the designated Google Form.
  3. The last date to upload the portfolios and the video is - 01 March 2026.
  4. The selected teams will be informed through email on or before - 02 March 2026.
  5. Top 5 teams will be selected based on their Google form submissions.

Round 2: Ramp Walk

  1. The teams selected from the Screening Round will walk the ramp for Couture ’26.
  2. A total of 10 minutes will be allotted for the performance and an additional 5 minutes will be allotted for stage setup.
  3. The stage setup time can be used for the performance.

Rules and Regulations:

  1. A team can consist of a minimum of 10 models and a maximum of 16 models, along with a maximum of 7 supporting crew members.
  2. All the team members must be from the same college.
  3. Participants must present a physical college ID card and PID to participate in the event.
  4. Online registration is mandatory for teams that qualify for the last round.
  5. Any form of vulgarity will lead to disqualification.
  6. The use of water, fire, or any kind of fireworks (party poppers) will lead to immediate disqualification.
  7. There is no gender restrictions for the team composition.
  8. Performance should be based on a theme of the team’s choice.
  9. Any deviation from a fashion-related choreography will result in a deduction of points.
  10. Violation of campus rules will lead to disqualification.
  11. Any form of intoxication on campus or in the green room will lead to disqualification.
  12. The decisions of the judges and organisers are final and binding.

Judging Criteria:

  • Coordination.
  • Music.
  • Confidence.
  • Gestures.
  • Creativity.
  • Garments.
  • Accessories.

name: Navarasa
description:
About the Event:

Lights, Camera, Drama! The spotlight is yours. Navarasa is a celebration of theatre where stories come alive and emotions take centre stage. From tragedy to comedy, and from timeless classics to powerful new narratives, performers explore the full depth of human emotion. Whether inspired by Kalidasa or driven by original storytelling, this is your moment to shine. Bring your passion, your story, and your creativity to the stage where emotions flow and stories soar under the lights.

Event Details:

Theme: Mukhavada or Ahankara

Round 1: Online Screening Round

  1. Participants must record their performance and upload it to Google Drive. The link of which must be shared via email to naxxxxxxxxxxxxxea@gmail.com under the subject "Navarasa Online Screening Submission".
  2. The video should be a 3-5 minute sample of the team’s performance, and it can be from any portion of the performance.
  3. Submission of edited videos is not allowed. The video must be shot in one continuous take.
  4. The deadline for submission of the video is - 28 February 2026.
  5. Kindly note that only recent recordings are accepted; the submission of old recordings is not permitted.
  6. A maximum of 9 teams will be selected from the online screening round and will proceed to the final round.

Note: All the rules of the final round apply to the online screening round as well.

Round 2: Final Round

  1. The act must strictly adhere to the theme.
  2. Each team will be allotted a total time of 15 minutes to cover stage setup, performance, and clearance.
  3. Each team may comprise 9+6 members. A maximum of 9 actors can be present on stage and a maximum of 6 members can be part of the stage support team (i.e., musicians, stage setup team, etc.).
  4. A performance could be done in any of these languages - Kannada, Hindi, Tulu, or English.
  5. Use of pre-recorded audio on stage is permitted only with prior approval from the organisers.
  6. Props may be brought and used.

Rules and Regulations:

  1. A team can comprise of 9+6 members. A maximum of 9 actors can be present on stage, and a maximum of 6 members can be part of the stage support team (i.e., musicians, stage setup team, etc.).
  2. All the team members must be from the same college.
  3. Participants must present a physical college ID card and PID to participate in the event.
  4. Targeting a specific religion, political party, personality, and use of foul language will lead to direct disqualification.
  5. Originality in scripting should be given the utmost priority. The implication of the theme is based on your creative perception.
  6. Improper use of theme or omission of the theme from the performance will result in a deduction in score or direct disqualification.
  7. The decisions of the judges and the organisers are final and binding.

Judging Criteria:

  1. Acting.
  2. Topic and creativity.
  3. Usage of properties.
  4. Stage presence.

name: Roadies
description:
About the Event:

Roadies is an adrenaline-pumping, brain-tingling multi-round event compiled to test attributes such as teamwork, physical endurance, mental sharpness, and resilience under high-stakes situations. A journey filled with challenges that push limits and beyond, where one shall rise to become the Ultimate Roadie.


Event Details:

Round 1: Team Task & MCQ Round

  1. Participants will compete in teams of 2 (Registration should be done individually).
  2. Each team must be formed by the participants themselves. If any participant is unable to form a team, the organisers will assign them to a team based on availability.
  3. Each team must attempt an MCQ test and subsequently perform a set of tasks.
  4. Eliminations will be carried out based on MCQ performance and task outcomes.


Round 2: Interview & Gang Selection

  1. Participants who qualify from Round 1 will be interviewed individually.
  2. Interviews will be conducted by the Gang Leaders.
  3. Based on the interviews, Gang Leaders will select participants to form their respective Gangs.
  4. Only selected participants will advance to the next round.


Round 3: Gang Task Round

  1. Participants will compete as part of the Gangs formed in Round 2.
  2. Each Gang will perform a series of physical tasks with guidance from their Gang Leader.
  3. Evaluation will consider both individual performance and overall Gang performance.
  4. Top-performing participants from all Gangs will be selected for the final round.


Round 4: Questionnaire & Stress Interview

  1. Participants will compete individually.
  2. Participants will be given a questionnaire to assess their thinking, decision-making, and personality.
  3. This will be followed by a stress interview.
  4. The final winner will be determined based on performance in this round.


Rules and Regulations:

  1. A team must consist of 2 members.
  2. All team members must be from the same college.
  3. Participants must present a physical college ID card and PID to participate in the event.
  4. The decisions of the judges and organisers are final and binding.
  5. The use of vulgar or offensive language, personal attacks on individuals regarding their character or physical appearance, and disrespectful behaviour towards the judges is strictly prohibited. 


 Judging Criteria:

  1. Physical fitness and endurance.
  2. Problem-solving ability.
  3. Communication skills.
  4. Professionalism and attitude.
  5. Ability to work in a team.

name: Robowars
description:
About the Event:

Witness the ultimate clash of engineering and strategy as 3 lb Beetleweight combat robots battle it out in a fierce competition. Equipped with spinning weapons, wedges, and flippers, these compact yet powerful machines push the limits of agility, durability, and precision. Prepare for an adrenaline-pumping spectacle where every match is a fight to the finish, and only the toughest robot emerges victorious!

Event Details: 

Design Specifications:

  1. The Beetleweight category permits all kinds of weapons specified in the rulebook.

  2. All the batteries should be on-board, only the weight of the remote controller will not be included.

  3. The weight of the bot will be checked before and/or after every match. 

  4. A bot can be in a ‘Cluster Bot’ formation. Each bot must meet the requirements described in this problem statement.

  5. The tolerance provided for such a bot will be as follows

    • Normal weight allowance 1.360kg (3 lbs.)
    • Multi bots (Cluster bots) 1.360 + 0.453kg (3+1 lbs.)
    • Non-traditional motion bonus 1.360+0.453kg (3+1 lbs.)

  6. Given one entry falls under the above said categories, then the max weight limit will be considered as 1.814 kg which is equivalent to 4lbs.

  7. More than 51% of the weight should be dedicated to the main bot and 31% to the multi bot.

  8. If a team is unable to get their multi bot ready, then they will be considered as normal weight class entry.

  9. One of the bots in a multi-bot setup should be a weapon bot to be considered as an entry to the competition. 

  10. Non Traditional Motion: 

    • Any robot that falls outside the definition of a ‘Traditional Motion System’ qualifies for the Non-Traditional Motion Bonus.
    • Traditional Motion Systems are classified as a robot that relies on rotational motion of a component in contact with the ground as its method of locomotion around the arena.
    • This includes all forms of wheels (round, non-circular, spoked, or offset-axis) as well as continuous tread, track or belt driven systems.
    • This also includes any robot that uses unpowered rotating objects (wheels, drums, rollers, ball bearings, etc.) as a means of friction reduction with the ground.
    • Anything other than these systems will be considered as Non-traditional motion systems.

Mobility:

All robots must have easily visible and controlled mobility in order to compete. Methods of mobility include the following: 

  1. Rolling (wheels, tracks, or the whole robot). 

  2. Non-wheeled robots have no rolling elements in contact with the floor and have no continuous rolling or Cam Operated motion in contact with the floor, either directly or via a linkage, but are not true walkers. Motion is continuous if continuous operation of the drive motor(s) produces continuous motion of the robot. Linear-actuated legs and novel non-wheeled drive systems are allowed under this category. 

  3. Jumping and hopping are allowed (manually operated). However, the maximum height of any part of the machine should not exceed 2ft during any stage of its jumping/hopping, and any damage caused due to its mechanism as well as the arena is the team’s responsibility. 

  4. Mobility methods that are not allowed: 

    • Flying (using airfoil, helium balloons, etc) is not allowed.
    • Robots should not secure themselves on the ring by using suction cups, etc.

  5. Immobility criteria: 

    • Once the bot seems immobile, the judge/referee will ask to show movement twice. If no movement is shown after that, a countdown of 10 seconds will start for the bot.
    • Each call out for showing movement will be a 5 seconds time frame.
    • In the event of immobility lasting beyond 2 minutes and 41 seconds, it shall not be classified as a knockout.
    • A linear movement of 60 cm should be shown to not be considered immobile.

Robot Control Requirements:

  1. All robots must be controlled through a wireless remote only, and all power supply must be onboard only. 

  2. A kill switch is mandatory for all robots. 

  3. Control must be exhibited over all of its functions and positions at all times and should be displayed even during matches as directed by the judges/organising team. 

  4. Although Autonomous functions within the bot are acceptable, the controller must be able to remotely disable or override those functions at any time. Also, note that any damage due to this function is the responsibility of the team, and there must compulsorily be a manual emergency stop (E-stop) function that should be controlled from the radio controller to manually override the autonomous function in case of emergency. Such an emergency shall be declared by the judge. 

  5. The team must have at least four frequency wireless remote-control circuits or two dual control circuits which may be interchanged before the start of the match to avoid frequency interference with other teams. Any instance of interference in the wireless system will not be considered for rematch or results. 

  6. Remote control systems available in the market can be used, while nonstandard or self-made remote-control systems must first be approved by the organisers and the judges. 

  7. The team should pair up the wireless remote with the robot before putting it into the arena. No extra time will be provided for pairing of transmitter and receiver once the robots are put inside the arena, and not connecting it prior to that may lead to disqualification. 

Battery and Power: 

  1. The robot should be powered electrically only. Use of IC engines in any form is not allowed. Onboard batteries must be sealed and immobilised-electrolyte types of batteries should be used (such as gel cells, lithium, NiCad, NiMH, or dry cells). 

  2. At any point in time, the electric voltage between any two points in the machine should not exceed 48V DC. Participants must bring their own converters for standard power supply according to Indian standards. All efforts must be made to protect battery terminals from a direct short as this would cause a battery fire, failure to do so will cause direct disqualification. In case of any emergency, the participants must stay calm and stay in their respective corners, the organisers will only be allowed inside the arena. 

  3. Use of damaged, non-leak-proof batteries may lead to disqualification. 

  4. Change of battery is not allowed during the match. 

Weapon Systems:

  1. Robots can have any kind of magnetic weapons, cutters, flippers, saws, lifting devices, spinning hammers etc. as weapons (if they qualify the criteria mentioned below). 

  2. All the weapons must have a safety cover over any sharp edges and a weapon lock to restrict the motion of the weapon when the bot is not in the arena. It should be removed only when the bot is ready on the arena. 

  3. Spinning Weapons:

    • Spinning weapons must come to a halt within 60 seconds of the power being removed using a self-contained braking-system.
    • Spinning weapons must only be tested in the arena, failing to adhere to this rule will lead to disqualification of the robot.
      • Spring-Loaded or flywheels: The spring must always be free and unloaded, only during the match the spring must be loaded inside the arena.
      • Weapons causing invisible or internal damage like Radio jamming, tasers, tesla coils, or any other high-voltage device are not allowed
      • Any kind of Tethered or un-tethered projectiles and hammer or thwack bots are not allowed.
      • Flame based and inflammable liquid-based weapons and lasers are not allowed. Any kind of explosive or intentionally ignited solid or potentially ignitable solid, usage of IC engines, Hydraulic and other flammable devices are not allowed.
      • Weapons used for entangling other bots like nets, cables, glue etc. not allowed. In case such Weapons are used, the bot will be disqualified.

  4. Arena Specifications:

    • Arena Dimensions: 8ft*8ft*8ft (length, breadth, height)
    • Protective Walls: All four sides are constructed from 6mm thick bulletproof polycarbonate to ensure maximum impact resistance

Rules for each round:

  1. A Double elimination form of the tournament will be followed in the competition. 

  2. The fixtures will be drawn by the judges in the presence of the organising team to ensure a fair process. This will be done using a chit system to assign opponents in the fixtures. 

  3. Fixtures will not be changed under any circumstances. Any request to do so will not be entertained by the organising team. 

  4. Match timings are absolute and under no circumstances will be extended unless it is the second final match. 

  5. Match timings will not be preponed under any circumstances as well.

  6. Please don't provide any excuse or arguments for not showing up on time because you have brought too many robots and you are unable to manage. Your entire team will be awarded 1 penalty point and forfeit for that match.


Match Frequency:

  1. Each robot shall be given 30 minutes between matches (Organisers reserve the right to change this duration on the day of the competition). If the team fails to return, with the robot ready, to the pre-match staging area when called after the allotted time, the team will be forced to forfeit as per the discretion of the judges and organisers. 

  2. Matches will be 3 minutes of active fight time exclusive of any time-outs. 

  3. Participants are strictly prohibited from entering the arena between matches. If a bot ceases to function, it will be declared immobile. However, if the judges determine that the bots are stuck together and no movement is possible from either side, the housebot will intervene to separate them. Additionally, if a bot becomes stuck against the wall, one unstick attempt per match will be permitted and executed by the housebot.

  4. Once a match has commenced, it will not be stopped under any circumstances, including fire, smoke, or other incidents, except in cases of a false start or a tap-out by a team. The match will only be halted if a team opts to tap out.

  5. In the event of significant damage to the arena or any other critical situations, the judges or organisers hold the authority to decide whether the match should be restarted or terminated.

Pre-Match Protocols:

  1. The robot should be ready, functional, and near the arena 30 minutes prior to the final call for the match. 

  2. Participating teams must adhere to strict weight rules, ensuring that the bot's total weight remains within the specified limits at all times. 

  3. Kill switch / U-link, radio failover, and weight limits are mandatory checks to be cleared by a team before the start of the match. 

Protocols during Match:

  1. During the match, a maximum of 3 people will be allowed near the arena on the robot driver's stage. The rest of the team must stay away from the arena and in the proper place designated by the organising team. 

  2. Participants are strictly prohibited from entering the arena under any circumstances. The organising team will address any mishap, and only after ensuring safety will teams be permitted to enter the arena to retrieve their robots. Failure to adhere to this rule will result in immediate disqualification, regardless of the match outcome, at the discretion of the organisers.

  3. The Weapon and the Robot should start moving only after the countdown is fully completed. If it is started in between the countdown, the judges and the organising team have the right to restart the match. A penalty point will be awarded to the team who has made the false start as well. 

Post-match Protocols:

  1. Judges may request teams to demonstrate the mobility and functionality of active weapons after the conclusion of a match if deemed necessary for determining the outcome, particularly in cases where the result is closely contested.

  2. Upon completing the inspection, the judge/referee will announce the opening of the arena. 

  3. Upon opening, the team should put the weapon lock first before turning off the kill switch. 

  4. Any team found to be opening the top of the robot for manually turning off the robot by disconnecting the battery will be awarded 1 penalty point. 

  5. Any team hitting the opponent after significant time passed after the announcement of the tap-out call will be awarded 2 penalty points.

Rules and Regulations: 

  1. A team must consist of 5 members.

  2. All the team members must be from the same college.

  3. Participants must present a physical college ID card and PID to participate in the event.

  4. Every team must have a unique name. The organising team reserves the right to reject entries from any team whose name it deems inappropriate, offensive, or conflicting. Organisers must be notified if a team changes its name. 

  5. Each team must specify their team representative (leader) at the time of registration on the website. All important communications between the organising team and the registered teams will be done through the team representative. The team representative must submit valid contact details (phone no, email ID, etc.) at the time of registration. 

  6. The robot's name cannot be changed during the whole course of the event. Any changes in the design should be informed to the coordinators/organising team. 

  7. The robot's name and photo should be submitted during the registration. The submitted details will be cross-checked anytime during the entire course of the event.

  8. If a team has more than one robot in a single category, they must be visually distinguishable, this shall be checked at the start of the tournament, and any deviation from the original shall not be allowed to participate.

  9. Visual aspects, including colour schemes, decals, and other details, will be evaluated.

  10. If a participating team is entering two bots in the same category, it's required that each bot has a distinct pilot, the same pilot cannot operate both bots. 

  11. All participating teams must present an abstract of the bot along with the bot they are competing with, one, two, or many. 

  12. All bots will be inspected according to the abstract submitted by the team and it should meet the specifications produced by the respective team. 

  13. All participating teams must have their bots completely assembled 30 mins prior to the start of the competition.

  14. The corners will be chosen through the fixtures directly. No coin toss or mutual understanding will be entertained in any case. 

  15. Testing of bots within the arena is strictly prohibited without prior approval from the organising team or judges.

  16. At least one of the members of the organising team or judge should be present while testing your bot. 

  17. No weapon testing is to be done inside the pits.

  18. The final weight verification will be conducted immediately before placing the bot in the arena. After the official weigh-in, team members are strictly prohibited from handling the bot.

  19. The bot with the highest points will be considered the judges' choice. A panel of 2 judges will evaluate the match, and the bot selected by at least two judges will be declared the winner. 

  20. The scorecards for all the matches will be public.

  21. When a judge’s decision is required, a recording of the fight will be watched by a panel of judges. If both judges choose the same winner, that bot will win the fight. If the judges choose different winners, a third tiebreaker judge will watch the same recording of the fight and choose the winner. 

  22. The decisions of the judges and the organisers are final and binding.

Judging Criteria:

A judge allocates 6 points to the competitors for each Control and Damage, and 5 points for Aggression. The bot with the highest total score is designated as the judges' choice. A panel of three judges will deliberate, and the bot selected by at least two judges will be declared the winner of the match.

When a judges’ decision is required, a recording of the fight will be reviewed by a panel of judges. If both judges select the same winner, that bot will be declared the winner of the fight. If the judges select different winners, a third tiebreaker judge will review the same recording and determine the winner.

  1. Aggression:

    • The intensity and frequency of intentional attacks, preferably with an active weapon.
    • To score points here, the bot needs to make attacks that could conceivably affect the opponent.

  2. Control:

    • Ability of the bot to dictate the match’s flow.
    • To score points here, a bot will be putting its opponent in a bad spot, like pinning it or getting it stuck.

  3. Damage:

    • The condition of the opponent’s bot at the end of a match compared to how it started.
    • To score points here, a bot needs to hurt its opponent’s critical systems.

Appeal System:  

  1. In case of an unfair match, any one of the 2 teams who played in that particular match can make an appeal to reconsider the decision. 

  2. Each team is given only 1 appeal for the whole tournament. 

  3. Once consumed, irrespective of whether the decision changed or not, the team will have no more appeals going forward in the tournament. 

  4. Once an appeal has been called, all the judges will review the footage, hear the statements provided by the appellant once, and take their decision. 

  5. The decision regarding the appeal will be communicated within 10 to 30 minutes of it being submitted.

  6. There is no guarantee that the old winner will be changed. 

  7. Following that, the judge’s decision will be final. 

Penalty System:

  1. Penalty points are given to the team upon violation of rules followed in the tournament. 

  2. A team can have a maximum of 3 penalty points before being considered as disqualified from the tournament. 

  3. An appeal can be used for this as well. However, it will be consumed anyhow.

  4. Penalty points are awarded according to the following criteria:

    • False start: - 1 point
    • Manually disconnecting the battery inside the arena without turning off the kill switch and weapon lock: - 1 point
    • Continued to hit the opponent more than once after the opponent has tapped out: - 2 points
    • Baseless arguments within teams or any other parties: - 1 or 2 points based on the severity of the situation
    • Violence or aggression shown outside the arena: - 3 points (No appeal can be used in this case).

Safety Rules:

  1. Proper activation and deactivation of robots is critical. Robots must only be activated in the arena, testing areas, or with the expressed consent of the event coordinators.

  2. In case of any accident/emergency, the organising team must be notified immediately. 

  3. The organising team will take steps to mitigate the issue, please wait for the same. Please remain calm in such a situation and wait for assistance to arrive from the health centre.

name: Talent House X
description:
About the Event:

Your talent is your identity—it’s what sets you apart from the rest. While everyone is born with a unique spark, not everyone dares to showcase it. Talent House X is your platform to bring that hidden brilliance to life. Whether it’s music, dance, art, or any other creative expression, this is your moment to shine. If you’ve discovered the X-factor within you, step onto the stage, own the spotlight, and leave the audience spellbound!

Event Details:

Round 1: Curtain Raiser

  1. Participants can only perform in the category of talent mentioned during the registration.
  2. Based on the scores allotted by judges, the shortlisted participants will move to the next round.
  3. Prior requirements for the performances (like mic, audio jacks, etc.) need to be brought to the notice of the organisers 2 days before the event (subject to availability).
  4. Participants will be given 4 minutes to complete their performance, and an extra 2 minutes for necessary stage arrangements and clearance.

Round 2: The Showdown

  1. Participants selected for this round must perform in the same category as mentioned during the registration.
  2. Participants will be given 7 minutes to complete their performance and an extra 2 minutes for necessary stage arrangements and clearance.

Rules and Regulations:

  1. Individual participation.
  2. Participants must present a physical college ID card and PID to participate in the event.
  3. Only the 'stated' talent at the time of registration is allowed for the first round. Otherwise, it remains the right of the organisers to call for direct elimination, unless it is clarified.
  4. Participants are not allowed to introduce themselves to the judges throughout the event.
  5. Participants must be present an hour before the commencement of the event and submit the songs and other media files in advance, if any, through a USB only.
  6. Participants must inform the organisers in advance if they are taking part in any other event during the time slot allotted to them to perform in Talent House X.
  7. Participants are not allowed to interact with the judges without the organisers’ permission.
  8. Vulgarity will not be entertained as an element and will result in direct elimination.
  9. Performances based on sensitive matters and political issues are strictly prohibited.
  10. Props can be used as per the participant's requirements. There is a strict prohibition on the use of fire, water, oil, colours, or smoke.
  11. Performances exceeding the given time limit will result in a deduction of points.
  12. Participants are responsible for the cleanliness of the stage after the performance.
  13. The decisions of the judges and the organisers are final and binding.

Judging Criteria:

  • Technical ability.
  • Creativity.
  • Professionalism.
  • Preparation and Presentation.

name: Art Duet
description:
About the Event:

Are you ready to face the rush of the timer together? How well do you know your teammate?

Ready for the trial of trust through art?

Event Details:

Round 1:

  1. Participants work together on one art sheet for 45 minutes.
  2. Twist - every 1 minute, teammates must take alternate turns to contribute to the sheet.
  3. Participants present and explain their artwork to the judges at the end of the round.

Round 2:

  1. Participants work separately on two different art sheets, but on the same topic.
  2. Each participant will be seated separately from their teammate.
  3. A total of 1 hour 30 minutes will be allotted to complete the artwork.
  4. Teams are given 1 minute to discuss their artworks among themselves.
  5. Participants then present and explain their artworks to the judges.

Rules and Regulations:

  1. A team must consist of 2 members.
  2. All the team members must be from the same college.
  3. Participants must present a physical college ID card and PID to participate in the event.
  4. The theme will be given on the spot.
  5. Open Medium: Paints are a must. Participants may use any type of paint, including acrylics, watercolours, or poster paints.
  6. Art sheets will be provided, but participants must bring their own painting supplies.
  7. Participants must finish within the time limit; no extra time will be provided.
  8. The decisions of the judges and organisers are final and binding.

Judging Criteria:

  • Creativity.
  • Presentation of the artwork.
  • Colour blending skills.

name: Digital Heist
description:
About the Event:

Step into an immersive digital adventure where curiosity leads the way. Navigate a live map, crack clever web and logic challenges, explore AR clues, and complete real-world tasks. Stay sharp, think fast, and outplay the trail in a thrilling race of skill and strategy.

Event Details:

Round 1:

  1. Round 1 will be conducted within a 2-hour overall window.
  2. Teams will attempt a series of puzzles, and each puzzle carries 40 points.
  3. A total of 6 hints will be provided for the round, and they may be used across puzzles without any point deduction.
  4. Each team will be allotted a maximum of 1 hour 30 minutes to complete the puzzles.

Round 2:

  1. Round 2 will be conducted for a total duration of 1 hour 30 minutes.
  2. Teams will attempt puzzles across multiple difficulty levels, including Easy (40 points), Medium (50 points), Hard (60 points), and Final Hard (100 points).
  3. The Final Hard puzzle includes a time-based bonus system, where completing it within 30 minutes, 1 hour or 1 hour 30 minutes awards +40, +20 or +10 points respectively.
  4. Hints will be available for all puzzles, and each hint used will result in a 15-point deduction.
  5. Puzzles are arranged on a graph-based map, and teams must unlock subsequent levels by solving the current one.
  6. If two teams land on the same puzzle, they may initiate a Speedrun Encounter with a 10-minute limit. The winning team earns +75 points, while the losing team incurs –50 points. The losing team may continue solving to regain +25 points, or exit to the lobby or solo mode. Quitting the encounter results in an additional –40 point penalty.
  7. The top 2 teams will be declared winner and runner-up, with ties resolved by the time taken to solve the final puzzle.

Rules and Regulations:

  1. A team must consist of 2 members.
  2. All the team members must be from the same college.
  3. Participants must present a physical college ID card and PID to be eligible to participate.
  4. Late arrivals will not be granted any additional time under any circumstances.
  5. Usage of Google Search and AI tools is permitted.
  6. Any form of communication (verbal or digital) with individuals outside the team is strictly prohibited.
  7. The decisions of the judges and organisers are final and binding.

Judging Criteria:

Round 1:

  • Scores earned by solving puzzles.
  • In case of a tie, the tiebreaker considers the time from signing in to solving the last puzzle.

Round 2:

  • Points are a combination of puzzle-solving, speed-run encounters, and hints.
  • In case of a tie, the tiebreaker considers the time of the last puzzle solved.

name: Hogathon
description:
About the Event:

The table is set and the challenge is on. Hogathon is an exciting food-eating showdown where speed, stamina, and appetite collide in timed, head-to-head rounds. So if you're up for the challenge, come show us just how big your appetite really is!


Event Details:

Round 1: Mass Elimination

  1. This round lasts approximately 90 minutes, depending on the number of participants.                                                                                                            

Round 2 & 3: Elimination Rounds

  1. These two rounds will have varying amounts of food for the participants to eat, within a fixed time limit of 1 hour per round.                                                    

Rules and Regulations:

  1. Individual participation.
  2. Participants must present a physical college ID card and PID to participate in the event.

  4. A participant must finish one item before moving on to the next.

  7. The decisions of the judges and the organisers are final and binding.

  • Neatness.
  • Time.

name: Improv
description:
About the Event:

Think you have what it takes to improvise your way to victory? If wit, humour, and spontaneity are your strengths, IMPROV is your stage to shine. Team up, think on your feet, and let your creativity steal the show as you tackle unpredictable situations with no scripts and no second chances.


Event Details:

Round 1: Escalation

  1. Two teams will compete in a given scenario, set either as a courtroom argument or a general debate.
  2. One participant from each team will begin by presenting their argument or viewpoint.
  3. At random intervals, another team member will enter the scene by selecting a line from a box.
  4. The entering participant must continue the argument using the selected line as the base.
  5. With each entry, the scene will escalate in intensity, drama, or absurdity.
  6. Teams will be evaluated based on creativity and seamless improvisation.         

Round 2: Emotional Atyachar

  1. Participants are divided into four emotional zones: Happy, Sad, Confused, and Angry.
  2. An everyday situation is given as a prompt, and each participant acts it out according to the emotion of the quadrant they are in.
  3. When the buzzer sounds, participants move to the next quadrant and instantly adapt their emotions while continuing the same scene.
  4. The challenge is to switch emotions smoothly and stay in character.                       

Tie breaker:

1. Something You Can Say To… But Not To…

A common scenario will be given to both teams.

One participant from each team will come forward to perform.

Participants must deliver a single statement that fits the scenario most creatively and unconventionally.

The statement must clearly reflect the given situation while maintaining relevance and originality.


2. Use the Word

  1. A baseline prompt is provided and the team begins improvising the scene.
  2. At a random point, an unexpected word is introduced by the MC.
  3. Participants must incorporate the word naturally into the ongoing performance.
  4. The word must be used without breaking character, flow, or continuity of the scene.                                                                                                                               

Rules and Regulations:

  1. A team must consist of 2 members.
  2. All the team members must be from the same college.
  3. Participants must present a physical college ID card and PID to participate in the event.
  4. All interactions must stay within the context of the provided scenario or topic.
  5. The decisions of the judges and organisers are final and binding.                                 

Judging Criteria:

  • Creativity and spontaneity.
  • Adaptability to changes.
  • Teamwork and flow.
  • Audience engagement.
  • Adherence to rules.

name: Lazzerena
description:
About the Event:

Lazzerena is a laser tag game which allows video game lovers to experience warzone scenarios in real life. It is played with guns which emit infrared beams. Infrared-sensitive sensors which are integrated on jackets are worn by each player. The game will consist of two teams, and each team will try to knock out the opponent by firing on their respective sensors.

Event Details:

  1. The game involves two teams, with a maximum of four members each.
  2. Two teams will be playing against each other, entering from two different entrances.
  3. Each team is equipped with laser-based handguns and has 3 lives.
  4. If a player loses all 3 lives, they are considered out.
  5. In order to win, players must either knock out all the opponents or must knock out the opposing team’s tower by shooting it 3 times within 7 minutes.
  6. Participants can be in the game until the opponent team is defeated.

Rules and Regulations:

  1. A team must consist of 4 members.
  2. All the team members must be from the same college.
  3. Participants must present a physical college ID card and PID to participate in the event.
  4. Two teams will be playing at a time, entering from two different entrances.
  5. Each team is equipped with laser-based handguns and has three lives.
  6. If any player loses all 3 lives, the player is out.
  7. To win, players must knock out all opponents using laser-based handguns or shoot the opponent team’s tower 3 times.
  8. Participants are expected to abide by ethical norms and rules of the event, with no tolerance for physical misconduct.
  9. Entry fee for each member of the team will be Rs 60 for the first-time entry.
  10. If any member of the team plays for the second time must pay only Rs 50.
  11. The decisions of the organisers are final and binding.

name: MELAS
description:
About the Event:

Get ready for an exciting and engaging quiz that brings Music, Entertainment, Literature, Arts, and Sports together on one stage. From popular hits to well-known stories, MELAS challenges your knowledge across familiar and exciting themes. Get set for a fast-paced journey through culture and creativity, where sharp minds take the spotlight.                                                                                   

Event Details:

Round 1 & 2:

  1. Each question in prelims carries 1 mark.
  2. Half marks are provided for partial answers.
  3. Questions with 2 parts in their answers receive half marks for each part being correct.
  4. The last 5 questions are the tiebreakers.
  5. There will be no negative marking.
  6. Blocks are allowed.
  7. Participants have 1 minute to answer each question.
  8. The combined score of Rounds 1 and 2, multiplied by 2, will be carried forward as the starting score for Round 3.                                                               

Round 3:

  1. A buzzer system will determine the order of answering.
  2. The first, second, and third teams to buzz correctly will be awarded 20, 16, and 14 points respectively, with subsequent teams receiving proportionately fewer points.
  3. An incorrect answer will result in a deduction of 5 points.                                             

Rules and Regulations:

  1. A team must consist of a minimum of 1 and a maximum of 3 members.
  2. All the team members must be from the same college.
  3. Participants must present a valid physical college ID card and PID to participate in the event.
  4. Registration must be done online through the website. On-spot registrations are not allowed.
  5. The number of teams qualifying for the subsequent rounds will be decided by the organisers. The rules for the block will be explained before the commencement of the quiz.
  6. The use of electronic gadgets is not allowed.
  7. Any sort of malpractice will lead to immediate disqualification.
  8. The quizmaster’s decision will be final and binding.                                                 

Judging Criteria:

  • The team with the highest score wins.

name: Movidea-Photography
description:

Frame it like you mean it! A photography competition where ideas turn into stories through light, motion, and perspective, inviting creators to capture moments that stand out.

name: Respawn-BGMI
description:
About the Event:

Gamers! Done with the slow, monotonous daily life?

If kicking a football gives you a real kick, or shifting gears leaves your blood pounding with the thrill of the chase, or perhaps the sound of the Vandal is enough to revive you after a long day...then you are not just a player, you are a gamer!

RESPAWN welcomes all the gamers to the battleground. Form up and show everyone your squad's synergy!


Rules and Regulations:

  1. The game will be played in a team of 4.
  2. Use of triggers or gaming consoles is not allowed; however, finger sleeves are permitted.
  3. Use of emulators and iPads are not allowed.
  4. Players should ensure their devices are compatible with the game and that they have the latest version installed.
  5. The matches will be played in the advanced room.
  6. The first match will be played on Rondo, and the subsequent matches will be a shuffle between Miramar and Erangel.
  7. The number of finishes will be awarded 1 point each. Position points will be based on the BGMI's points table released by the organisers.
  8. Total points for the team will be decided by considering position points and the number of kills.
  9. If any player is found teaming up or using any modification of the BATTLEGROUNDS MOBILE INDIA game client, the team will be disqualified from the tournament.
  10. The number of finishes will be given priority if there is a tie between the teams.
  11. Participants must present a physical college ID card and PID to participate in the event.
  12.  The registration fee for the event is ₹400 per team.


Rounds:

Preliminary Round:

  • Classic Erangel will be played with 16 teams.
  • The top 16 teams based on the points table will continue to move on to the next round till the finals.

Finals:

  • The top 16 teams will compete in LAN Grand Finals following standard BGMI competitive rules.

name: Stomp That
description:
About the Event:

One stage, one track, and all eyes on your crew as teams go head-to-head, stomping the floor with sharp moves, clean timing, and serious group chemistry. It’s fast, competitive, and all about how well you move together, so if your squad’s got the energy and confidence, pull up and prove it.


Event Details:

Round 1: Group Dance Performance

Note: There is no separate category for western and eastern.

  1. A total of 6+2 minutes is allotted for the performance, including stage setup.
  2. Each team performs their choreography within the allocated time.


Rules and Regulations:

  1. A team must comprise a minimum of 6 members, with no maximum limit.
  2. All the team members must be from the same college.
  3. Participants must present a physical college ID card and PID to participate in the event.
  4. The participants must be ready at the venue at least 45 minutes prior to the commencement of the event.
  5. The music must be submitted to the organisers in a USB drive 30 minutes before the event, and if live music is used, it should be informed prior to the event.
  6. Any kind of vulgarity will lead to immediate elimination.
  7. The use of fire, powder, oil, and water is strictly prohibited.
  8. Participants must maintain a respectful and positive attitude towards all competitors, judges, and organisers.
  9. The decisions of the judges and the organisers are final and binding.


Judging Criteria:

  1. Choreography and coordination.
  2. Expression and creativity.
  3. Costume riginality and overall impression on the audience.
  4. Incorporation of the theme.

name: Tulu Tulipu
description:
About the Event:

Step into the vibrant world of Tulu Tulipu, where your knowledge, quick thinking, and passion for the Tulu language and Tulunadu are put to the test. A perfect blend of learning, excitement, and unforgettable moments awaits you!

Event Details:

Round 1: Eliminator Round

  1. A set of multiple-choice questions and one-word answer type of questions will be given.

  2. Each team answers these questions within the given time.

  3. Questions will be based on Tulu language, history, heritage, and culture of Tulunadu.


Round 2: Sheet of Fate

  1. Participants will be presented with a challenge designed to test their ability to decipher and comprehend information.

  2. Different questions or clues will be displayed in a PowerPoint presentation.

  3. The questions will be based on general knowledge of Tulunadu and the Tulu language.


Rules and Regulations: 

  1. A team must consist of 2 members.

  2. All the team members must be from the same college.

  3. Participants must present a physical college ID card and PID to participate in the event.

  4. The decisions of the judges and organisers are final and binding.


Judging Criteria:

Round 1:

  • MCQ question answers

Round 2:

  • Questions answered correctly

name: Usaravalli
description:
About the Event:

Usaravalli is a Kannada turncoat event where participants speak on a given topic and switch their stance midway from supporting it to opposing it without stopping or breaking flow! It’s a real test of clarity, confidence, and control when the script suddenly flips. If you can sell both sides without missing a beat, this is your challenge!


Event Details:

Round 1:

  1. The topic will be disclosed in the event hall, and participants will be given 10 minutes to prepare before the competition begins.
  2. Each participant has 4 minutes to speak, of which 2 minutes are allocated for presenting arguments in opposition.


Round 2:

  1. In this round, participants will select a topic on the spot and will be allotted 2 minutes for preparation.
  2. Each participant will have 4 minutes to speak. Upon the ringing of the bell, they must switch their stance to present a different perspective on the topic.


Rules and Regulations:

  1. Individual participation.
  2. Participants must present a physical college ID card and PID to participate in the event.
  3. Only Kannada is allowed; use of any other language is prohibited.
  4. The content must not be offensive towards any religion, caste, gender, or community. Violations may lead to disqualification by the organisers.
  5. Each speech, including both stances, must be completed within the allocated 4 minutes.
  6. Participants will have 10 minutes to prepare after receiving the topic.
  7. The decisions made by the judges and the organisers are final and binding.


Judging Criteria:

  • Content of speech.
  • Smoothness of transition between stances.
  • Language.
  • Voice modulation and articulation.
  • Physical presence such as eye contact, body language, etc.

name: Vibe
description:
About the Event:

The floor is set, the lights are loud, and this is where you prove you belong. Bring sharp moves, full control, and the confidence to go head-to-head with the best. Two intense rounds, with no room to fake it; only those who adapt and deliver make it through. Step in, level up, and earn your win on the dance floor!


Event Details:

Round 1: Cypher Solo

  1. Each participant has 60-90 seconds to perform.
  2. Participants must freestyle to the music provided on the spot; pre-choreographed routines are not allowed.


Round 2: The Final Showdown

  1. Participants face off in a dance battle.
  2. Battles can be one-on-one or three-way face-offs, depending on the number of finalists.
  3. Songs are played randomly, requiring participants to adapt and showcase their skills on the spot.
  4. The first dancer performs until the buzzer sounds, after which the second dancer must immediately take over and continue dancing to the same track. Each turn lasts 30 seconds.
  5. After each battle, the judges decide the winner based on performance. The losing participant will be eliminated, and the winner will advance further.
  6. The number of battles will be 2, but 1 more battle will be conducted if asked by the judges.


Rules and Regulations:

  1. Individual participation.
  2. Participants must present a physical college ID card and PID to participate in the event.
  3. Use of props is not allowed.
  4. Participants must adhere to the time limits strictly.
  5. Participants must respect the Cypher setup, refrain from obstructing or interrupting others, and maintain a positive and respectful attitude towards competitors, judges, and organisers. Any unsportsmanlike behaviour will result in disqualification.
  6. The number of participants that will be shortlisted for the second round depends on the total number of entries.
  7. The decisions of the judges and the organisers are final and binding.


Judging Criteria:

Round 1:

  • Expression, creativity, musicality, stage presence, and overall performance will be considered.

Round 2:

  • Entertainment factor, creativity, spontaneity, and crowd engagement will be considered.

name: Bob the Builder
description:
About the Event:

Are you ready to transform basic materials into remarkable masterpieces? Collaborate, unleash your creativity, and construct your path to success, allowing your imagination to lead the way!


Event Details:

Round 1: Aptitude Round

A total of 60 minutes is allocated for the aptitude test.

The teams with the highest scores advance to the next round.


Round 2: The Builders’ Challenge

  1. Miniature bricks, ice cream sticks, cardboards, and clay will be provided.
  2. Participants must construct models according to a given plan.
  3. A total of 2 hours will be allotted for model construction.


Rules and Regulations:

  2. All the team members must be from the same college.
  3. Participants must present a physical college ID card and PID to participate in the event.

  • Round 2: Aesthetic appearance and accurate dimensions of the model.

name: Bomb Squad
description:
About the Event:

Test your logic, speed, and presence of mind in a race to defuse a simulated bomb, where quick thinking meets the ultimate test of time. One mission. One countdown. Do you have what it takes to defuse it?


Event Details:

Round 1: Aptitude Round

Teams solve a questionnaire featuring puzzles, verbal and non-verbal questions, along with aptitude-based and basic electronics questions.


Round 2: Defuse the Bomb!

  1. Teams take turns defusing the bomb within a set time limit.
  2. A set of technical and aptitude-based questions must be solved by teams to determine the correct wires to disconnect before the time runs out.
  3. Each wrong disconnection incurs a time penalty.


Rules and Regulations:

  1. A team must consist of 2 members.
  2. All the team members must be from the same college.
  3. Participants must present a physical college ID card and PID to participate in the event.
  4. The decisions of the judges and the organisers are final and binding.


Judging Criteria:

  • Round 1: Correctness of answers to the questions.
  • Round 2: Time management and efficiency in defusing the bomb.

name: Code Relay
description:
About the Event:

Code Relay is where minds race, ideas collide, and teamwork takes centre stage. It’s a high-stakes dance of logic and speed, where every second counts and collaboration fuels the fire. Ready to conquer the clock and leave your mark?

Event Details:

Round 1: 

  1. Each team is given a coding problem to solve.
  2. The problem given can be related to algorithms, data structures, or mathematical concepts.
  3. Participants may use their own laptops and preferred coding environments for implementation.
  4. Team members work together to break down the problem and implement a solution.
  5. Teams must divide the work, but only one person will be allowed to interact with the coding interface at a time.
  6. After completion, teams submit the solution via the designated platform or file-sharing method.

Round 2:

  1. Each team participates in a "relay" format, where members solve a part of a coding challenge sequentially, passing the baton to the next member.
  2. The challenge consists of multiple smaller coding problems.
  3. Each team member works on different problems, or one problem is divided into smaller tasks.
  4. Each member must solve their part independently, and after completing their task, they will pass the baton to the next member.
  5. Members will be assigned specific portions of the problem, and they cannot assist each other directly during their turn.
  6. The team must submit the entire solution after the last member completes their section. Only one submission per team will be accepted.

Rules and Regulations:

  1. A team must consist of 2 members.
  2. All the team members must be from the same college. 
  3. Participants must present a physical college ID card and PID to participate in the event.
  4. The decisions of the judges and the organisers are final and binding.

Judging Criteria:

  1. Correctness of the solution. 
  2. Time taken to complete the task. 
  3. Code quality and efficiency (e.g., readability, optimisation). 
  4. Overall teamwork and collaboration.

name: Escape Room
description:
About the Event:

Prepare for an immersive challenge where your detective skills are put to the test. With few technical and problem-solving skills, you must escape the grasp of your kidnapper. Your basic knowledge of biology and chemistry will be the key to uncovering the room's secrets. Enter the room, decode who did it, and escape!

Event Details: 

Round 1: 

Part 1: Screening test

  1. It consists of a questionnaire comprising topics from the fundamental sciences (physics, chemistry, and biology). 
  2. A total of 30 minutes is allotted to complete the questionnaire.
  3. Top 10 teams advance further.

Part 2: Protocol hunt

  1. Teams scavenge for clues that will lead them to the escape room.

name: Locked in Reality
description:
About the Event:


Locked in Reality is an exhilarating technical event that challenges participants to utilize their programming, analytical, and problem-solving skills to overcome a series of engaging puzzles and tasks.   2. Each game represents a stage that teams must unlock by solving technical, logical, or analytical challenges within a specified time limit.

name: LogiCide
description:
About the Event:

Enter LogiCide, a crime-themed, mystery-driven logic challenge where patterns conceal the truth. Participants decode sequences, connect clues, and apply structured analytical reasoning across multiple rounds. Only teams that identify hidden logic and reason consistently will progress towards the final revelation.


Event Details:

Round 1:

  1. Teams will solve logic-based problems involving pattern identification, sequence analysis, quantitative conditions, and output prediction using simple pseudocode or logical steps.
  2. Only the top-performing teams from this round will qualify for the next round.

Round 2:

Part A: Black Box Logic Decoding

  1. Teams will be given three to four Black Box questions.
  2. In each question, teams will receive a set of input-output pairs and one input without an output.
  3. Teams must identify the underlying pattern or logic used in the given pairs and determine the correct output for the unseen input.
  4. The outputs obtained from all the questions together will form a final clue.

Part B: Algorithm Reconstruction

  1. Teams must reconstruct and present the decoded logic by drawing a flowchart and writing pseudocode.
  2. The flowchart and pseudocode must be clear, complete, and consistent with the logic identified in Part A.
  3. Judges may test the solutions using additional hidden inputs to verify correctness.


Rules and Regulations:

  1. A team must consist of 2 members.
  2. All team members must be from the same college.
  3. Participants must present a physical college ID card and PID to participate in the event.
  4. Use of external tools such as mobile phones is strictly prohibited.
  5. The decisions of the judges and organisers are final and binding.


Judging Criteria:

Round 1:

  • Logical reasoning and analytical thinking.
  • Pattern identification and sequence analysis.
  • Quantitative aptitude involving conditions and constraints.
  • Output prediction using simple pseudocode or logical steps.

Round 2:

Part A: Black Box Logic Decoding

  • Correctness and generality of the code.
  • Logical consistency across all inputs.
  • Clarity of explanation through comments.

Part B: Algorithm Reconstruction

  • Logical correctness of the flowchart
  • Clarity and completeness of decision paths
  • Accuracy of pseudocode reconstruction
  • Consistency between flowchart and pseudocode

name: Mission: Oppenheimer
description:
About the Event:

Step into Mission: Oppenheimer, where intellect meets intensity in a race against time.

Tackle rapid-fire quizzes and high-stakes challenges that push your Data Science and AI skills to the limit under pressure.


Event Details:

Round 1: Quiz and Bounty Round

Quiz Round:

  1. A total of 20 questions will be given.
  2. The duration of the quiz is 15 minutes.
  3. Questions will be based on Data Science and Artificial Intelligence.
  4. One point will be awarded for each correct answer.
  5. The top 8 teams will proceed to the next sub-round.

Bounty Round:

  1. A website will be provided to each team.
  2. The website will contain a bounty which, when discovered, will lead to a unique access key.
  3. The time of successfully entering the access key will be considered as the tiebreaker.
  4. The top 6 teams will proceed to the next round.

Round 2: Task-Based Round

Envelope Round:

  1. Teams will be given an envelope containing a hint pointing to a location outside the lab and within the college.
  2. At the indicated location, a volunteer will provide another envelope with a new hint.
  3. There will be only four envelopes.
  4. In case of a tie, the team that reaches first and answers a riddle correctly will receive the envelope.

Task Round:

  1. Teams must choose between two types of tasks based on their strengths.
  2. Upon completion of the task, teams must identify the next location and proceed accordingly.
  3. All teams will proceed to the next sub-round.

Bomb Round:

  1. At the final location, teams will be provided with a hint and a system.
  2. Teams must identify the correct folder based on the hint.
  3. The folder will contain a problem scenario and an Excel file to be analysed using Data Science.
  4. The bomb will be activated ten minutes after the last team reaches the lab.
  5. The team that cuts the wires in the correct order before time runs out wins the game.
  6. In case of a tie, the team that cuts the maximum number of correct wires in the least time will be declared the winner.


Rules and Regulations:

  1. A team must consist of a minimum of 2 and a maximum of 3 members.
  2. All team members must be from the same college.
  3. Participants must present a physical college ID card and PID to participate in the event.
  4. The decisions of the organisers are final and binding.


Judging Criteria:

Round 1:

  • Eight teams proceed based on quiz scores, with time considered as the tiebreaker.
  • Six teams proceed to Round 2 based on the time of entering the access key.
  • In case of a tie, the time of submission will be considered as the tiebreaker.

Round 2:

  • Four teams proceed based on successful completion of the Envelope Round.
  • The winning team is determined based on bomb detonation or the maximum number of correct wires cut in the least time.

name: Robo Race
description:
About the Event:

Gear up for an electrifying Robo Race, where creativity meets engineering excellence! Witness robots race through challenging tracks that test speed, control, and precision at every turn. Packed with obstacles designed to push both machines and minds to their limits, this event is not just about crossing the finish line—it’s about innovation, strategy, and technical mastery. Build smart, race hard, and prove your dominance in the ultimate robotic showdown!


Event Details:

Bot Specifications:

  1. The bot’s dimensions should not exceed 30 cm x 30 cm x 25 cm (l x b x h).
  2. The bot’s weight should not exceed 3 kg. However, a tolerance of 5% is acceptable.
  3. The potential difference between any two electrical points on the bot must not exceed 12 volts throughout the run.
  4. The bot can be powered on board or off the board.

Round 1:

  1. Bots navigate terrain with obstacles such as humps and elevations.
  2. The bot to cross the finish line the quickest will be qualified for the next round.
  3. If a bot topples, or goes out of the track or is touched by hand, then it must start from the previous checkpoint.

Round 2:

  1. Bots face several difficult terrains and will have to perform a few tasks.


Rules and Regulations:

  2. All the team members must be from the same college.
  3. Participants must present a physical college ID card and PID to participate in the event.
  4. An individual cannot be a member of more than one team.
  5. Teams must construct their own robots; ready-made kits are not allowed.
  6. Robots must adhere to the provided specifications. Any deviation will result in disqualification.
  7. Both wired and wireless robots are permitted.
  8. A bot cannot be shared by multiple teams.
  9. AC supply will not be provided.
  10. No practice runs are allowed on the main track.
  11. The team completing the track in the least time wins.
  12. The bot structure cannot be changed during the competition.
  13. If a bot falls or becomes immobile, it will be reset to the beginning of the obstacle with a penalty.
  14. Limited technical timeouts will be allowed for technical issues.
  15. Pulling bots with wires on the track is strictly prohibited.
  16. Bots must remain intact until results are declared.
  17. The organisers will not be responsible for any kind of electromagnetic interference in wireless communication.
  18. The time measured by the organisers will be final.
  19. Organisers reserve the right to modify rules and rounds on the day of the event as they see fit.
  20. Any misconduct or violation of rules by participants may lead to disqualification.
  21. The decisions of the judges and the organisers are final and binding.


Judging Criteria:

  • Time taken to cross the finish line.
  • Task performance.
  • Penalties will be applied wherever necessary.

name: Robo Soccer
description:
About the Event:

Step into the thrilling world of Robo Soccer, where technology meets competition! Showcase your skills as machines take the spotlight, navigating the arena with precision and strategy. It’s a battle of bolts and bytes, redefining the future of sports and innovation!

Event Details:

After the closure of on-spot registrations, team captains will have the opportunity to select slots. The fixture details will be promptly displayed thereafter. Once the fixtures are established based on the chosen slots, no changes will be permitted.

Match Details:

  1. In the beginning, the ball will be kept in the middle of the arena.

  2. The match will consist of two halves. The side will be decided by the toss.

  3. The duration of each half will depend on the type of match as follows:

    • Initial knockout match: 3 minutes.
      • Each half will be of 1.5 minutes.
      • Court change after the first half.
    • Quarter-final: 3 minutes.
      • Each half will be of 1.5 minutes.
      • Court change after the first half.
    • Semi-finals and Final: 5 minutes.
      • Each half will be 2.5 minutes.
      • Court change after the first half.

  4. 1-minute break will be given during the court change in semi-finals and finals only.

  5. Based on the number of teams, the time constraints may be changed.

  6. Golden Goal: In case of a draw, whoever scores the first goal will be considered the winner.

  7. The soccer bot can only transform to its size at the beginning, it cannot be divided into multiple parts later.

  8. The weight of the bot will be checked before starting each match. Once the weight of the bot is finalised, no modifications to the weight will be allowed.

  9. Technical timeout: If the bot is immobilised during the match, the team will first be given 60 seconds to fix it without any loss of points.

  10. If the team fails to fix it in 60 seconds, another 60 seconds can be given at the expense of 1 point.

  11. If the team does not repair the bot within this time, then it will be disqualified.

  12. Stalling tactics of any kind will not be tolerated.

  13. All the bots must have their own power supply.

  14. The referee will analyse bots before each match and only after their approval can the bot enter the match. They have the right to reject the bots, taking into consideration the rules and dimension limits.

  15. The match will be paused in case of any entanglement of wires of both bots. If the ball is immobile for 10 seconds, then the game will be reset, and the ball will be declared as a common ball.

  16. The ball should not be lifted in the air by the bot.

  17. In case a team is disqualified, the opponent team wins the match by default.

  18. The dimensions provided in the rules must be followed for the bots to participate.

  19. Ready-made kits/Lego models are not allowed.

  20. Only 3 members of each team are allowed to be present at a time in the arena.

  21. If the bot is wired, one member will be the controller of the bot, and the other will hold the wire.

  22. The structure of the robot should not change during the competition (e.g., if you have a wedge at the front, you can't convert it into a claw or vice versa).

  23. Organisers will not be responsible for any kind of electromagnetic interference in the wireless communication.

  24. One member of the team must be present near the arena, or in the room provided at any given time.

  25. Teams must be ready before the time mentioned in fixtures.

  26. A warning call will be given every 2 minutes from the time given for the team, after the third call, the team will be disqualified.

  27. The bot should not be disassembled until the results are declared.

  28. If a foul is committed, and a goal occurs before the play is restarted due to the foul, the goal will not be counted.

  29. Pulling the bot with connected wires on the arena will lead to disqualification.

  30. The organising team and the judges have full authority to change any of the above rules as per the circumstances.

    Bot Specifications:

    1. Bots can be wired or wireless. Wireless bots should have a minimum range of 12 feet.

    2. Wires must be sufficient to reach all corners of the arena.

    3. The potential difference between any two electrical points on the robot must not exceed 12 volts throughout the run.

    4. Gripping mechanism is not allowed.

    Bot Dimensions:

    1. Length <= 30 cm.

    2. Breadth <= 30 cm.

    3. Height <= 30 cm.

    4. A total of 5% tolerance is allowed on length, breadth, and height.

    5. Weight: 5 kg (tolerance of 10%).


Rules and Regulations:

    1. A team must consist of 4 members.
    2. All the team members must be from the same college.
    3. Participants must present a physical college ID card and PID to participate in the event.
    4. The competition will involve a 1 vs 1 matchup between the bots.
    5. Teams must arrive on time, and any anticipated delays must be conveyed to the organisers in advance.
    6. Fixture assignments will be determined through the slot selection process. The need for a loser's bracket will be decided by the organisers based on the total number of participants.
    7. In case of any disputes, the decisions of the referees or event managers will be final.
    8. The decisions made by the judges and the organisers are final and binding.


    Judging Criteria:

    • Each goal scored by a team will result in 4 points being awarded.
    • A warning will be given for not following the rules, and 2 points will be deducted for each subsequent warning.
    • The winner of the competition will be declared based on the points scored.

  7. The rounds continue as the winners from each set compete with each other and finally, two teams are selected for the final round.

name: Lakshman Rekha
description:
About the Event:

Innovation thrives where speed meets discipline. Build a high-speed wireless bot engineered to master a challenging track with precision. Whether in a solo run or a head-to-head duel, every curve of the arena challenges your design, and every millisecond exposes your mastery.


Event Details:

Round 1: Track Challenge

  1. Bots will have to navigate a unique track, the details of which will be revealed on the day of the event.

Round 2: Advanced Track Challenge

  1. Bots compete on a more complex track with additional challenges.


Rules and Regulations:

  1. A team must consist of 3 members.
  2. All the team members must be from the same college.
  3. Participants must present a physical college ID card and PID to participate in the event.
  4. Each round will feature a unique map, revealed on the day of the event, with round-specific rules explained just before the start.
  5. Only self-built bots are allowed; ready-made bots are strictly prohibited, and robots cannot be shared between teams.
  6. All arenas will have a black line/trajectory on a white surface, approximately 3 cm wide.
  7. Once a bot starts, it must remain fully autonomous; any external control will result in disqualification.
  8. The dimensions of the bot should not exceed 20 cm x 20 cm, and participants must arrange their own batteries and charging equipment.
  9. Bots veering off the path or failing to complete the course will incur penalties.
  10. The decisions of the judges and the organisers are final and binding.


Judging Criteria:

  • Build, efficiency, and speed in navigating the track.
  • Score = Time taken to finish + Penalties.

name: MAD AD
description:
About the Event:

A stage where imagination meets madness. Mad Ad invites you to turn ordinary ideas into extraordinary advertisements through quick humour, clever twists, or heartfelt stories. Bring your ideas, sell your story, and own the spotlight.


Event Details:

Round 1: Online Screening Round

  1. As part of the screening process, participants are required to submit their scripts to the organisers for evaluation by 20 February 2026.
  2. The submissions will be reviewed and the selected teams will be notified by 25 February 2026.


Round 2: 

  1. Participants must come prepared with an advertisement for a product or service of their choice.
  2. A total duration of 5+2 minutes is allotted for the advertisement.
  3. Props are not allowed.
  4. The advertisement can be in English, Kannada, Tulu, or Hindi.


Rules and Regulations:

  1. A team can consist of a minimum of 5 members and a maximum of 8 members.
  2. All the team members must be from the same college.
  3. Participants must present a physical college ID card and PID to participate in the event.
  4. The Ad must not contain any obscene language or material that may offend the beliefs or sentiments of any culture, language, religion, or institution.
  5. Any form of vulgarity observed during the competition will result in immediate disqualification of the team.
  6. Negative marking will be imposed for any violation of the rules.
  7. The organisers reserve the right to make any changes to the event as they see fit.
  8. The decisions of the judges and the organisers are final and binding.


Judging Criteria:

  1. Ability to capture and retain audience attention.
  2. Clarity and effectiveness of the ad concept.
  3. Collaboration and teamwork.
  4. Creativity and originality.
  5. Use of humour.
  6. Efficient time management.

name: Meme War
description:
About the Event:

A challenge to collaboratively craft the funniest, most clever, and supremely shareable memes centred around a specific theme or topic, all within the dynamic synergy of a team.



Event Details:

Round 1: 

  1. Teams are provided with meme templates at the beginning of the competition.
  2. Participants must create and submit memes within the allocated time.


Round 2:

  1. Teams must select one meme from the submissions.
  2. The chosen meme will then be recreated in video and audio format.


Rules and Regulations:

  1. A team must consist of 2 members.
  2. All the team members must be from the same college.
  3. Participants must present a physical college ID card and PID to participate in the event.
  4. The decisions of the judges and the organisers are final and binding.


Judging Criteria:

  1. Relevance of the theme. 
  2. Creativity and originality: The uniqueness and innovation demonstrated in meme creation and video recreation. 
  3. Humour and entertainment value. 
  4. Criteria unique to round 2: 
                a. Visual appeal.
                b. Adherence to the original meme's essence.
